'''Ella Jones''' (born 1955) is an American [[Chromatography|chromatographer]], pastor, and politician who serves as the 12th mayor of [[Ferguson, Missouri]]. A former member of the [[Ferguson, Missouri|Ferguson]] City Council, Jones is the first African-American and woman elected mayor of the city.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|first=Andy |last=Rose|title=Ferguson elects first black mayor in city's history|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/03/politics/ferguson-first-black-mayor-ella-jones/index.html|access-date=2020-06-03|website=CNN|date=3 June 2020 }}</ref><ref name=":1"/>

== Education ==
Jones earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in chemistry from the [[University of Missouri–St. Louis]].

== Career ==
Prior to entering politics, Jones was a high-pressure liquid chromatographer. She worked at the [[Washington University School of Medicine]] and [[KV Pharmaceutical]] before becoming a sales director with [[Mary Kay]]. In April 2015, Jones was elected to the [[Ferguson, Missouri|Ferguson]] City Council, where she represented the city's first ward.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/two-black-candidates-elected-ferguson-city-council-n337626|title=Two Black Candidates Elected to Ferguson City Council|publisher=NBC News|date=April 7, 2015|accessdate=September 9, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=About us – Ella Jones for Mayor of Ferguson|url=https://ellamjonesformayor.com/about-us/|access-date=2020-06-03|language=en}}</ref> In February 2020, Jones was selected to serve on the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]] Local Government Advisory Committee.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-02-25|title=EPA Administrator Appoints Ferguson, Missouri, City Council Member Ella M. Jones to EPA Local Government Advisory Committee on Small Community Subcommittee|url=https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/epa-administrator-appoints-ferguson-missouri-city-council-member-ella-m-jones-epa|access-date=2020-06-03|website=US EPA|language=en}}</ref>

In the 2017 municipal election, Jones ran for mayor, receiving 42.77% of the vote. It was the city's first election after the [[shooting of Michael Brown]] and subsequent [[Ferguson unrest]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stlouisco.com/Portals/8/docs/document%20library/elections/eresults/el170404/el45.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405130406/http://www.stlouisco.com/Portals/8/docs/document%20library/elections/eresults/el170404/el45.htm|archive-date=2017-04-05|title=St. Louis County, Missouri}}</ref>

In the June 2, 2020, mayoral election, Jones defeated fellow council member Heather Robinett. Jones succeeded incumbent [[James Knowles III]], a Republican who was unable to seek re-election due to term limits.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Schlinkmann|first=Mark|title=Ella Jones becomes the first African American and first woman elected mayor of Ferguson|url=https://www.stltoday.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/ella-jones-becomes-the-first-african-american-and-first-woman-elected-mayor-of-ferguson/article_4fcddeed-9586-571c-b88a-bbcae3c71f70.html|access-date=2020-06-03|website=STLtoday.com|date=3 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Ferguson elects its first black and first woman mayor|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ella-jones-ferguson-elects-first-black-first-woman-mayor-michael-brown-protests/|access-date=2020-06-03|website=www.cbsnews.com|date=3 June 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref> On June 17, 2020, Jones was sworn in as the first black and female mayor of Ferguson.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.kmov.com/news/ella-jones-sworn-in-as-first-black-woman-mayor-of-ferguson/article_efdcb0a0-b108-11ea-a563-6738c47d4b88.html|title=Ella Jones sworn in as first Black woman mayor of Ferguson|first=Alexis|last=Zotos|publisher=KMOV4|date=June 17, 2020|accessdate=August 7, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Rosenbaum|first=Jason|title=Ferguson Elects Its First African American Mayor|url=https://news.stlpublicradio.org/post/ferguson-elects-its-first-african-american-mayor|access-date=2020-06-04|website=news.stlpublicradio.org|language=en}}</ref> On April 4 2023, Jones was re-elected as mayor of Ferguson, winning a second term by 21 votes.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.firstalert4.com/2023/04/05/ferguson-mayor-wins-3rd-term-by-21-votes/|title=Ferguson Mayor wins 2nd term by 21 votes|publisher=[[KMOV|First Alert 4]]|date=April 5, 2023|accessdate=September 9, 2025}}</ref>

She is also a pastor in the [[African Methodist Episcopal Church]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|last=Medina|first=Jennifer|date=2020-06-03|title=Ella Jones Is Elected First Black Mayor of Ferguson|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/03/us/politics/ella-jones-ferguson-mayor.html|access-date=2020-06-03|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Jones moved to [[Ferguson, Missouri]] with her husband, Tim. Tim Jones died in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ruiz|first=Michelle|title=Ferguson Mayor Ella Jones on Making History and the Power of Black Female Leaders|url=https://www.vogue.com/article/ella-jones-ferguson-missouri-mayor-interview|access-date=2020-08-16|website=Vogue|date=July 2020|language=en-us}}</ref> Jones has one daughter.<ref name=":1" />
